title: WPSB/164/2012 of SUJEET KUMAR SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 164 of 2012
Sujeet Kumar Singh .............. Petitioner
State of Uttarakhand and others .............. Respondents

Present: Mr. Kishore Kumar, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Standing Counsel for the State/
 respondent No.1.
 Mr. Vinay Kumar, Standing Counsel for Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut
 Nigam Limited/respondent Nos. 2 to 4.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
BARIN GHOSH, C.J. (Oral)
 The Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Board has a
procedure for recording of annual confidential reports. Clause (5)
thereof directs determination of adverse remarks. In that, it has
been provided that the competent officer or the officer nominated
by him will determine as to which entry/remark or part thereof is
adverse. The said Clause further provides that while determining
the same, the competent officer or the officer nominated by him
shall be guided by the sub-clauses of Clause (5) thereof. Clause 6
of the said procedure provides for communication of adverse
remarks. Petitioner was adjudged as very good for a particular
period. For the next period, he received blank entry. Thereafter,
he received good entry for two periods; then again a blank entry.
Thereafter satisfactory for three entries; then good, then again
very good, very good, blank, very good, very good, very good.
Because of these few good entries and satisfactory entries, he did
not receive 60 marks being the basic cut off for being promoted.
He, accordingly, made a representation stating that the entries for
the relevant periods, which earned him much less marks, were not

2
communicated to him as is the mandate in the Government Order
dated 30th September, 2010 and, accordingly, those entries be
communicated to him, so that he can make an appropriate
representation. In response to the said representation, it was held
out to the petitioner that the Government Order is not applicable
to the Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Limited and it has its own
rules and purported to insinuate that, in terms thereof, there being
no adverse remark, there was no scope of communicating the
same and since the petitioner has not received the benchmark of
60, he has been found unfit to be promoted. The learned Standing
Counsel is appearing on behalf of Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam
Limited. We asked him to show us determination by the
competent officer or the officer nominated by him as to which
entry/remark or part thereof, in so far as the petitioner is
concerned, was adverse. He submitted that no exercise to that
effect was made and, accordingly, there is nothing on record. In
other words, he purported to contend that though there is a
provision for determination of adverse entry/remark, but since
obligation pertaining thereto has not been discharged, there is no
adverse entry/remark. This submission is patently illegal, unjust
and absolutely incorrigible. A person getting satisfactory and good
carrying much less marks, but, at the same time, has been
adjudged to be very good carrying very high marks will not be
communicated that he has received such poor remarks, because
the competent officer or the officer nominated by him had no time
to determine, whether those low mark confidential reports would
be treated as adverse or not? We flay the stand taken by
Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Limited and declare that the action
on its part, as depicted above, is anti employees of the
Corporation.
2. We, accordingly, allow the writ petition and hold or
determine on behalf of the competent officer that each good and

3
satisfactory entry received by the petitioner for the relevant period
was and should be deemed to be adverse and, accordingly, the
same should be communicated separately to the petitioner as
adverse entries entitling him to make representations against the
same. Such entries must be communicated to the petitioner with
full materials and support thereof within a period of fifteen days
from today, whereupon the petitioner shall be entitled to give a
reply or representation in respect of each such entry within a
period of one month from today. In the event, on the
representation of the petitioner, those entries are altered and the
petitioner secures the benchmark of 60, his case for promotion
shall be reconsidered in a Departmental Promotion Committee to
be held solely for the petitioner and if the petitioner is found
suitable for being promoted, he shall be given promotion with
notional effect from the date when others were found suitable for
being promoted in the Departmental Promotion Committee held
on 14th December, 2011. It is made clear that while
communicating the adverse entries, as referred to above, it must
be indicated by the final authority as to how and why very good
and very good grade given respectively by reporting officer and
reviewing officer could be treated by him as blank.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C.J.)
 08.07.2013 08.07.2013
P. Singh
